- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after recent spikes, then sharply drop — suggesting overshoot and failure to capture mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window, particularly when true values show a slow upward or sideways trend.
- Forecast bias is stronger in periods with high volatility or sharp price drops — model fails to adjust downward quickly enough.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price declines — often takes 2–3 days to correct downward bias.
- When true prices show a clear downward trend, model often forecasts a plateau or slight uptick — fails to recognize trend continuation.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — forecasts spike after minor price movements, then fails to correct.
- In low-volatility periods, model tends to underestimate prices — especially when recent history shows stable or slightly declining values.
- Model often fails to capture the “tail” of a price correction — underestimates the depth of a drop or the speed of recovery.
- Forecast horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are prone to overconfidence in early days, then underconfidence in late days — suggesting a non-linear decay in forecast accuracy over time.
